structure_display.line: Drawn as a ring, as allulose is in water: D-psicofuranose, the five-membered ring, drawn as fructose is. The SMILES and identifiers are PubChem's open-chain record of the same sugar.
structure_display.model_line: The model shows alpha-D-psicofuranose, the commoner of the two five-membered forms; in water the two interconvert at the ring carbon that carries two oxygens.

why_it_matters.text: A rare sugar found in figs and raisins that tastes like sugar and browns like sugar, but passes through the body largely unmetabolized.

description: A rare sugar found in figs and raisins that tastes like sugar and browns like sugar, but passes through the body largely unmetabolized.

parts.label: The hydroxyl group
parts.sentence: An O-H on a carbon that is not part of an aromatic ring, the group that makes a molecule an alcohol. It both gives and accepts hydrogen bonds, which helps the molecule mix with water.

parts.label: The hemiacetal
parts.sentence: One carbon bonded to a ring oxygen and to an O-H. In water this ring can open and close again, which is how sugars such as glucose switch between their forms.

parts.label: The ring system
parts.sentence: Rings joined where they share atoms, or a single ring standing alone. Atoms in a ring are held in place, so this part keeps its shape while chains around it can bend.
